authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The company completed the spin-off of its New York Rangers business by distributing all shares of MSG Rangers Corp. to its stockholders. It now owns and operates the Knicks business and has been renamed MSG Knickerbockers Corp.

The company, MSG Rangers and certain subsidiaries entered into a Transfer Consent Agreement with the NHL. It requires NHL consent for future transfers of Rangers ownership or location, and the parties released the NHL entities from claims.

The board was reduced in size, and five directors resigned effective at the Distribution date to become directors of the spun-off company. The distribution has since occurred, but the evidence does not separately confirm the board change took effect.

business_model.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: The company owns and operates the New York Knicks (NBA) and a development league team, the Westchester Knicks. It distributed its Rangers hockey business to stockholders after the quarter ended, so the Knicks are now its sole major franchise.
quotes: MSG Knickerbockers Corp. is a leading professional sports company that owns and operates the New York Knicks (NBA), as well as a development league team, the Westchester Knicks (NBAGL).

business_model.claim: The company reports one segment, so the evidence gives no segment split.
quotes: The Company operates and reports financial information in one segment.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from several streams: ticket sales, a share of suite rental fees, league media distributions, sponsorship and signage, food and beverage, merchandise, and local media rights fees from MSG Networks. This describes the fiscal 2026 10-K business, which included both teams.
quotes: We earn revenue from several primary sources: ticket sales and a portion of suite rental fees at The Garden, our share of distributions from NHL and NBA league-wide national and international media contracts and other league-wide revenue sources, sponsorships and signage, food and beverage sales at The Garden and merchandising.
We also earn substantial fees from MSG Networks for the local media rights to telecast the games of our sports teams.

business_model.claim: Ticket sales have historically been the largest single revenue source. Tickets are sold through season plans, group sales and single games, and single-game prices are set dynamically.
quotes: Ticket sales have historically constituted our largest single source of revenue.

business_model.claim: The company receives an equal share of league-wide national and international media rights fees, which it describes as a significant recurring revenue stream.
quotes: The Company receives a pro-rata share of fees related to the NBA’s and NHL’s national and international media rights agreements, which provide a significant recurring revenue stream for the Company.
Fees paid by telecasters under these arrangements are pooled by each league and then generally shared equally among all teams.

business_model.claim: Local media rights fees from MSG Networks were a meaningful but shrinking revenue stream in fiscal 2026: $125.7 million, or 11% of total revenues, versus $157.4 million, or 15%, in fiscal 2025. These figures cover both teams.
quotes: In fiscal year 2026, we recorded $125.7 million of local media rights revenues, which represented 11% of our total revenues in fiscal year 2026, compared to $157.4 million in fiscal year 2025, which represented 15% of our total revenues.

business_model.claim: A 2025 amendment to the local telecast agreements cut fees by 28% for the Knicks and 18% for the Rangers, with no annual rights fee escalators. This is a driver of lower local media revenue.
quotes: fee reductions of 28% for the Knicks and 18% for the Rangers, both effective as of January 1, 2025, with no annual rights fee escalators

business_model.claim: Under the Arena License Agreements with MSG Entertainment, the Knicks get 35% of suite and club license revenue and 50% of net profits from food and beverage at their games. They pay MSG Entertainment a 30% commission on merchandise sold at The Garden. The company does not own the arena, so arena-linked revenue is shared with a related party.
quotes: Pursuant to the Arena License Agreements, the Knicks and the Rangers are entitled to 35% and 32.5%, respectively, of the revenues received by MSG Entertainment in connection with suite and club licenses.
Pursuant to the Arena License Agreements, the Knicks and the Rangers receive 50% of net profits from the sales of food and beverages during their games at The Garden.
Pursuant to the Arena License Agreements, the Knicks and the Rangers pay MSG Entertainment a commission equal to 30% of revenues from the sales of their merchandise at The Garden.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and the 10-Q balance sheet footnote.
business_model.claim: Playing at The Garden is also a fixed cost. The teams owe fixed annual license fees to MSG Entertainment through June 2055. At Sep. 30, 2026, $807,619 of noncurrent operating lease liabilities (table in thousands) was payable to MSG Entertainment, out of $831,373 in total.
quotes: The Arena License Agreements provide for fixed payments to be made from inception through June 30, 2055 in 12 equal installments during each year of the contractual term.

As of September 30, 2026, Operating lease liabilities, current and Operating lease liabilities, noncurrent included balances of $52,103 and $807,619, respectively, that are payable to MSG Entertainment.

business_model.claim: The largest costs are player and other team personnel salaries. The NBA salary floor limits how far these can be cut, and a soft cap with exceptions lets a team pay more than the cap.
quotes: Our most significant expenses are player and other team personnel salaries.

business_model.claim: NBA league mechanics add large costs. For fiscal 2026 the Knicks recorded luxury tax expense of $44,437 and net revenue sharing provisions of about $66,065 (table in thousands).
quotes: For the 2025-26 and 2024-25 seasons, the Knicks were a luxury tax payer and we recorded luxury tax expense of $44,437 and $38,035, respectively, for fiscal years 2026 and 2025.
Our net provisions for revenue sharing, net of escrow, for fiscal year 2026 were approximately $66,065.

business_model.basis: Seasonality is stated in the 10-K. The balances are from the 10-Q statements.
business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal. It is concentrated in the second and third fiscal quarters, so the September quarter shows an operating loss and large movements in deferred revenue and cash. In that quarter deferred revenue rose to 366,415 from 165,416 at Jun. 30, 2026, and cash used in operations was 146,268 (tables in thousands).
quotes: due to the NBA and NHL playing seasons, revenues from our business are typically concentrated in the second and third quarters of each fiscal year

business_model.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q.
business_model.claim: First-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue was $45.5 million, up $6.0 million or 15%. The company reported an operating loss of $25.5 million. The main revenue drivers were league distributions, up $3.1 million, and food, beverage and merchandise sales, up $2.6 million. These results include the Rangers.
quotes: For the fiscal 2027 first quarter, the Company generated revenues of $45.5 million, an increase of $6.0 million, or 15%, as compared to the prior year period.
This primarily reflected higher revenues from league distributions of $3.1 million, mainly due to an increase in certain league distributions unrelated to national media rights fees.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Team success feeds revenue. Playoff games add revenue, and the Knicks' 2025-26 NBA Championship boosted merchandise demand in the latest quarter.
quotes: When our sports teams qualify for the playoffs, we also benefit from the attendance and in-game spending at the playoff games.
primarily due to higher Knicks merchandise revenues driven by ongoing demand from the team winning the 2025-26 NBA Championship

business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative expense is the largest operating cost line in the latest quarter, at $60.8 million against revenue of $45.5 million. It includes $3.6 million of spin-off transaction expenses. Direct operating expenses were $8.8 million.
quotes: This increase was primarily driven by (i) expenses related to the spin-off transaction in the current year period of $3.6 million and (ii) higher other general and administrative expenses, partially offset by (iii) lower employee compensation and related benefits of $1.2 million.

business_model.basis: Taken from the 10-Q balance sheet and cash flow statement; the link between the draw and the cash outflow is inferred.
business_model.claim: The seasonal cash outflow was partly funded by revolver borrowing. The company drew 40,000 on its revolving credit facilities, and long-term debt rose to 282,000 from 242,000 (tables in thousands).

competitive_position.claim: The Knicks are an original NBA franchise with a long history of success, including the 2025-26 NBA Championship. The filings present this as the core of the company's franchise position.
quotes: As an original franchise of the NBA, the Knicks have a rich history, winning three NBA Championships including the 2025-26 NBA Championship.

competitive_position.claim: The company's home-arena position is secured by a long-term licence from MSG Entertainment, and it does not own The Garden. That gives it long-dated access to a large-market arena but leaves it dependent on a related party.
quotes: The Arena License Agreements have a term of 35 years and expire in June 2055.
We do not own The Garden.

competitive_position.claim: A large share of revenue is contracted on a multi-year basis (media rights, suites, sponsorship), which the company says moderates the year-to-year effect of team performance.
quotes: The year-to-year impact of team performance is somewhat moderated by the fact that a significant portion of our revenue derives from media rights fees, suite rental fees and sponsorship and signage revenue, all of which are generally contracted on a multi-year basis.

competitive_position.claim: First-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue was $45.5 million, up $6.0 million or 15% from the prior year period. The company attributes much of the rise to league distributions and merchandise.
quotes: For the fiscal 2027 first quarter, revenues of $45.5 million increased $6.0 million, or 15%, as compared to the prior year period.

competitive_position.claim: Merchandise demand rose after the championship: food, beverage and merchandise sales were up $2.6 million, mainly on Knicks merchandise.
quotes: In addition, food, beverage and merchandise sales increased $2.6 million as compared to the prior year period, primarily due to higher Knicks merchandise revenues driven by ongoing demand from the team winning the 2025-26 NBA Championship.

competitive_position.claim: The quarter was still loss-making: operating loss was $25.5 million (improved $2.0 million, or 7%) and adjusted operating loss was $20.0 million (improved $0.8 million, or 4%).
quotes: the Company reported an operating loss of $25.5 million, an improvement of $2.0 million, or 7%

competitive_position.claim: Revenue is seasonal: the company says it is typically concentrated in the second and third fiscal quarters, so first-quarter results alone say little about the full-year position.
quotes: due to the NBA and NHL playing seasons, revenues from our business are typically concentrated in the second and third quarters of each fiscal year

competitive_position.basis: stated in the statements; the link to seasonality is inferred from the seasonality text in P3
competitive_position.claim: Liquidity tightened in the quarter (balance sheet figures in thousands): cash fell to 40,046 from 164,511 and long-term debt rose to 282,000 from 242,000, including 40,000 drawn on revolving credit facilities. This limits the company's financial room.

Local media rights revenue depends on MSG Networks, whose fees to the Knicks were cut by 28% in a restructuring. The local agreements now end after the 2028-29 seasons, and the filings name a default or bankruptcy of MSG Networks as a risk.
quotes: were amended to effect fee reductions of 28% for the Knicks and 18% for the Rangers, both effective as of January 1, 2025, with no annual rights fee escalators

competitive_position.claim: Player costs and the NBA luxury tax weigh on the Knicks. They were a luxury tax payer for 2025-26 and, on the current roster, would be again for 2026-27.
quotes: Based on the current roster, the Knicks would also be a luxury tax payer for the 2026-27 season.

competitive_position.claim: The Knicks face direct competition in the New York market: another NBA team (the Nets), other leisure options, and possible NBA expansion that would dilute equally shared national media revenue.
quotes: we must compete with another NBA team located in the New York City metropolitan area (the Nets) as well as with other NBA teams and the NBA itself

Because revenue from national media rights agreements is divided equally among all NBA and NHL teams, any further expansion would dilute the revenue realized by the Knicks and/or the Rangers from such agreements.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the concentration point is inferred
competitive_position.claim: After the Rangers spin-off the company is a single-franchise Knicks business. This concentrates its exposure on the Knicks' performance, though first-quarter figures still include the Rangers.
quotes: distributed all of the issued and outstanding shares of the common stock of MSG Rangers to its stockholders
consolidated results include the financial results of the Rangers business

competitive_position.claim: The company has large related-party ties: lease liabilities payable to MSG Entertainment, and overlapping executives with other Dolan-linked companies, which the filings flag as conflict risk.
quotes: James L. Dolan will serve as the Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Registrant, MSGS Spinco, MSG Entertainment and Sphere Entertainment.

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet and cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Cash fell sharply in the quarter: 40,046 (table in thousands) at September 30, 2026, against 164,511 (table in thousands) at June 30, 2026, a net decrease of 124,465 (table in thousands) in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash.

financial_health.basis: figures stated in the balance sheet; the settlement mechanism is inferred from the revenue-recognition description in the 10-K MD&A
financial_health.claim: Current liabilities of 652,763 (table in thousands) exceed current assets of 285,849 (table in thousands), a working capital deficit. Deferred revenue of 366,415 (table in thousands) is the largest current liability, and league-related accruals are 130,860 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet and cash flow statement; the link between the draw and the operating cash use is inferred
financial_health.claim: Reported debt is 16,500 (table in thousands) current plus 282,000 (table in thousands) long-term. Long-term debt rose from 242,000 (table in thousands) after 40,000 (table in thousands) of proceeds from revolving credit facilities in the quarter.

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet and its footnote
financial_health.claim: Balance sheet leverage is high. Total liabilities of 1,833,986 (table in thousands) exceed total assets of 1,526,541 (table in thousands), and total equity is (307,445) (table in thousands). Operating lease liabilities are 58,682 (table in thousands) current and 831,373 (table in thousands) noncurrent, mostly payable to MSG Entertainment (52,103 and 807,619, table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: figures stated in the cash flow statement; the seasonal interpretation is inferred from the MD&A seasonality statement
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was negative and worse than a year earlier: net cash used in operating activities was (146,268) (table in thousands), against (84,954) (table in thousands). The largest swings were accrued and other liabilities of (184,302) and prepaid expenses and other assets of (78,671), partly offset by deferred revenue of 200,971 (all table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: stated in the income statement, MD&A table and earnings release
financial_health.claim: Earnings do not cover financing costs this quarter. Operating loss was (25,457) (table in thousands), adjusted operating loss was (20,004) (table in thousands), and net loss was (31,137) (table in thousands). Interest expense was (4,699) (table in thousands). Non-cash add-backs are small, with share-based compensation of 3,953 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Cash was also used for financing items: 16,966 (table in thousands) of taxes paid in lieu of shares issued for equity-based compensation, against 8,770 (table in thousands) a year earlier. No dividends were paid in the quarter.

financial_health.basis: stated for the current debt balance and the risk language; the funding sources are inferred from the balance sheet and cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Refinancing and funding: the current portion of debt is 16,500 (table in thousands). Cash of 40,046 (table in thousands) and the revolver are the visible sources to meet it. The filings flag possible need for additional financing.
quotes: We may require additional financing to fund our ongoing operations, the availability of which is highly uncertain.
a default by our subsidiary under its credit facility

financial_health.claim: Revenue timing supports later liquidity: revenues are concentrated in the second and third fiscal quarters, so the first-quarter cash burn sits in the weak part of the year.
quotes: In addition, due to the NBA and NHL playing seasons, revenues from our business are typically concentrated in the second and third quarters of each fiscal year.

financial_health.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 8-K
financial_health.claim: The September 30, 2026 balance sheet still includes the Rangers business, which was distributed on October 26, 2026. It therefore does not show the post-spin-off cash, debt or lease position.
quotes: The accompanying unaudited consolidated interim financial statements include the financial results of the Company’s Rangers business in continuing operations for all periods presented.
Subsequent to the Distribution, the Registrant will no longer include the financial results of the Spinco Business for the purpose of its own financial reporting.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release and 10-Q MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Reported top-line growth is the base of the thesis: first-quarter revenue rose $6.0 million, or 15%, to $45.5 million. The operating loss was still $25.5 million. Whether this continues depends on the same revenue lines recurring in later quarters.
quotes: For the fiscal 2027 first quarter, revenues of $45.5 million increased $6.0 million, or 15%, as compared to the prior year period.

growth_thesis.basis: The amount and attribution are stated; whether it recurs is not stated.
growth_thesis.claim: League distributions were the largest identified revenue driver, adding $3.1 million. The release attributes this to certain league distributions unrelated to national media rights fees. For it to continue, those distributions must recur; the evidence does not say they will.
quotes: This primarily reflected higher revenues from league distributions of $3.1 million, mainly due to an increase in certain league distributions unrelated to national media rights fees.

growth_thesis.basis: The attribution is stated in the release; persistence is inferred from the risk-factor language.
growth_thesis.claim: Merchandise and other sales added $2.6 million, driven by demand from the 2025-26 NBA Championship. For this to continue, championship-driven fan demand must persist.
quotes: In addition, food, beverage and merchandise sales increased $2.6 million as compared to the prior year period, primarily due to higher Knicks merchandise revenues driven by ongoing demand from the team winning the 2025-26 NBA Championship.
There can be no assurance that any of our sports teams, including the Knicks and the Rangers, will maintain continued popularity or compete in post-season play in the future.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and risk factors; the effect on future results is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Playoff participation is a named upside driver that this quarter does not show. It requires the Knicks to keep qualifying and advancing.
quotes: When our sports teams qualify for the playoffs, we also benefit from the attendance and in-game spending at the playoff games.
The Knicks last qualified for the post-season during the 2025-26 NBA season and the Rangers last qualified for the post-season during the 2023-24 NHL season.

growth_thesis.basis: Balances and policy are stated; the link to future revenue is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Multi-year contracted revenue streams support the revenue base, and deferred revenue rose to 366,415 (table in thousands) from 165,416 at June 30, 2026. Conversion to reported revenue requires the company to perform on contracts as the season is played.
quotes: The year-to-year impact of team performance is somewhat moderated by the fact that a significant portion of our revenue derives from media rights fees, suite rental fees and sponsorship and signage revenue, all of which are generally contracted on a multi-year basis.

Amounts collected for ticket sales, media rights, suite licenses and clubs, sponsorships, and venue signage in advance of the Company’s satisfaction of its contractual performance obligations are recorded as deferred revenue and are recognized as revenues when earned.

growth_thesis.basis: Contract term and sharing rule are stated; the effect on Knicks revenue is not quantified.
growth_thesis.claim: National NBA media rights are a contracted growth base. The new NBA agreements took effect with the 2025-26 season and run through 2035-36. This holds as long as the league renews or replaces contracts and expansion does not dilute the equal per-team share.
quotes: The NBA’s agreements with The Walt Disney Company, NBCUniversal and Amazon, which took effect starting with the 2025-26 season, will expire following the 2035-36 season.

Because revenue from national media rights agreements is divided equally among all NBA and NHL teams, any further expansion would dilute the revenue realized by the Knicks and/or the Rangers from such agreements.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release and 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Cost containment contributed to the smaller operating loss: net provisions for league revenue sharing and NBA luxury tax fell $3.0 million, and operating loss improved $2.0 million to $25.5 million. This requires player payroll and luxury tax obligations to stay contained.
quotes: a $3.0 million decrease in net provisions for league revenue sharing expense (net of escrow and excluding playoffs) and NBA luxury tax
Based on the current roster, the Knicks would also be a luxury tax payer for the 2026-27 season.

growth_thesis.basis: Amounts are stated; whether the spin-off costs end is inferred and not confirmed.
growth_thesis.claim: Adjusted operating loss improved $0.8 million, or 4%, to $20.0 million, helped by higher revenue and partly offset by $3.6 million of spin-off transaction expenses in selling, general and administrative expenses. If those costs are non-recurring, the underlying improvement would not be offset by them in later periods. The evidence does not say.
quotes: This increase was primarily driven by (i) expenses related to the spin-off transaction in the current year period of $3.6 million and (ii) higher other general and administrative expenses, partially offset by (iii) lower employee compensation and related benefits of $1.2 million.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release, MD&A and 8-K.
growth_thesis.claim: The Rangers spin-off completed on October 26, 2026, and this quarter's consolidated results still include the Rangers business. The reported 15% growth therefore may not describe the Knicks-only company, and a growth thesis must be re-based on post-spin results.
quotes: As a result of the timing of the spin-off, the Company’s fiscal 2027 first quarter consolidated results include the financial results of the Rangers business.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors; these figures cover the company before the spin-off.
growth_thesis.claim: The local media rights stream is a condition, not a driver, for the thesis. It fell last fiscal year to $125.7 million from $157.4 million after rights-fee cuts, and it continues only if MSG Networks keeps paying under agreements that run to the end of the 2028-29 seasons.
quotes: In fiscal year 2026, we recorded $125.7 million of local media rights revenues, which represented 11% of our total revenues in fiscal year 2026, compared to $157.4 million in fiscal year 2025, which represented 15% of our total revenues.

growth_thesis.basis: Balances are stated; the seasonal reversal is inferred from the MD&A seasonality statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Funding is a condition for continued operations: cash fell to 40,046 (table in thousands) from 164,511 and long-term debt rose to 282,000 from 242,000. For this to be sustainable, seasonal cash inflows must follow and the revolving credit facility must remain available.

material_events.claim: The company completed the spin-off of its New York Rangers business by distributing all shares of MSG Rangers Corp. to its stockholders. It now owns and operates the Knicks business and has been renamed MSG Knickerbockers Corp.
quotes: On October 26, 2026, the Registrant distributed all of the issued and outstanding shares of the common stock of MSG Rangers to its stockholders (the “Distribution”).

material_events.claim: The company, MSG Rangers and certain subsidiaries entered into a Transfer Consent Agreement with the NHL. It requires NHL consent for future transfers of Rangers ownership or location, and the parties released the NHL entities from claims.
quotes: The Registrant parties and MSG Rangers parties also agreed to release the NHL entities from any claims against them.

material_events.basis: inferred from the contingent wording in P8 and the completed Distribution in P6
material_events.claim: The board was reduced in size, and five directors resigned effective at the Distribution date to become directors of the spun-off company. The distribution has since occurred, but the evidence does not separately confirm the board change took effect.
quotes: Effective as of the Distribution date, the Board of Directors of the Registrant has decreased the size of the Board of Directors from 15 to 12 directors.

material_events.claim: The company amended and restated the employment agreement of Executive Chairman and CEO James L. Dolan. It acknowledges that he will also be employed by MSG Rangers.
quotes: On October 26, 2026, the Registrant amended and restated the existing employment agreement with James L. Dolan, the Registrant’s Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (the “Amended and Restated Dolan Employment Agreement”).

material_events.claim: Jamaal T. Lesane became Executive Vice President and Chief Legal Officer and ceased to be Chief Operating Officer.
quotes: Effective September 21, 2026, Jamaal T. Lesane became Executive Vice President and Chief Legal Officer of Madison Square Garden Sports Corp. (the “Company”) and ceased to serve as the Company’s Chief Operating Officer.

risks.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q statements. The seasonal reading is inferred from the deferred revenue change and the MD&A seasonality description. The 10-K risk factor predates the spin-off, and the quarterly risk factors section was not found.
risks.claim: Cash fell to 40,046 from 164,511 (table in thousands) in the quarter. Operating activities used 146,268 and 40,000 was drawn on revolving credit facilities. Long-term debt rose to 282,000 from 242,000.
quotes: We may require additional financing to fund our ongoing operations, the availability of which is highly uncertain.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors. The 10-K covers both teams. The packet does not show the Knicks-only local media amount after the Rangers spin-off.

quotes: The NBA and NHL have also imposed significant restrictions on amounts of financing and/or certain types of financings and the rights of those financing providers.

risks.basis: Receivable and revenue figures are stated. The seasonal timing is an inference, and the 8-K/A confirms the overlap but says nothing about any dispute.
